observation_summary: The SimplexSolver was returning an incorrect solution because it failed to correctly handle cases where multiple variables were associated with the same basic row in the Simplex tableau, leading to incorrect coefficient values.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves replacing an incorrect, inefficient, and flawed nested-loop logic (which attempted to check for duplicate basic rows by inspecting tableau entries) with a robust set-based tracking mechanism (`HashSet<Integer> basicRows`). This is a fundamental change to the algorithmic procedure used to extract the solution from the tableau, correcting the logic for identifying and handling dependent variables. It is not a simple guard (Checking) or a single value assignment (Assignment/Initialization), but a rewrite of the computational strategy for extracting the result.
evidence_used: The fix_diff_oracle shows the removal of a nested loop that checked tableau entries and the introduction of a HashSet to track basicRows.
The bug report indicates the solver arrived at an incorrect solution (0.0 instead of 1.0).
The logic change directly modifies how the 'coefficients' array is populated, which is the core computational step of the method.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds a check (`if (basicRows.contains(basicRow))`), the primary issue is the underlying algorithmic approach to identifying and handling multiple variables associated with the same basic row, which was previously handled by an incorrect nested loop.
The fix does not involve correcting associations between different objects or data structures, but rather corrects the internal logic of a single method within the SimplexTableau class.
